evals.name: api-boundary-crash
evals.expected_output: Identifies that `as User` is an unchecked claim and the real fix is runtime parsing at the fetch boundary (Zod or similar, type inferred from schema). Also flags that lastLoginAt is a string over JSON not a Date, and that the optional-field state bag should be a discriminated union so `user` present implies not loading and no error. Working code, not just advice.
assertions: Identifies `await res.json() as User` as the root cause — an unchecked claim — rather than framing it as a null-safety problem
Introduces runtime schema validation (Zod, Valibot, ArkType or equivalent) at the fetch boundary
Derives the TypeScript type from the schema (e.g. z.infer) instead of maintaining a hand-written interface alongside it
Flags that `lastLoginAt: Date` is wrong because JSON carries a string, and coerces it at the boundary
Replaces the optional-field state bag with a discriminated union over a status field
Checks `res.ok` before parsing the response body
Does not offer optional chaining or non-null assertions as the primary fix

evals.name: js-to-ts-migration-plan
evals.prompt: i inherited a node/express service at work - about 120 js files, commonjs, no types at all, jest tests that mostly pass. mix of route handlers, a db layer using knex, and a big utils folder. leadership wants typescript but we cant stop shipping features for a sprint to do it. whats the actual play here? i've done greenfield ts before but never a conversion this size and i dont want to end up with a half-migrated mess that everyone resents
evals.expected_output: A phased, incremental plan: checkJs/allowJs first for value with zero churn, coexistence verified through the build/test pipeline, leaf-first conversion order (constants -> domain types -> db layer -> logic -> routes), strictness ratcheted flag by flag with noImplicitAny before strictNullChecks, @ts-expect-error over @ts-ignore with a suppression ratchet in CI, honest placeholders (unknown over invented types), and guardrails so it doesn't slide back. Explicitly avoids a big-bang rewrite.
assertions: Recommends incremental coexistence via allowJs rather than a big-bang rewrite or a dedicated migration sprint
Recommends checkJs (and/or JSDoc types) to get type-checking value before converting any files
Specifies a leaf-first conversion order — utilities, constants and domain types before route handlers
Ratchets strictness flag by flag (noImplicitAny before strictNullChecks) rather than enabling strict globally at the start
Prefers @ts-expect-error over @ts-ignore, or proposes a suppression count that may only decrease
Requires `tsc --noEmit` as its own CI gate, noting that transpilers strip types without checking them
Warns against inventing types for shapes not yet understood, preferring unknown or a narrow partial type

evals.name: async-sync-script
evals.expected_output: Catches the three real bugs: sequential awaits in the loop (should be bounded-concurrency parallel, capped near the vendor's 20/sec limit, NOT unbounded Promise.all), forEach with an async callback that never awaits (so the writes float and the script reports done before they finish), and the top-level sync() call with no .catch so rejections go unhandled and the cron sees exit 0. Should also add per-request timeout/AbortSignal, retry with backoff for transient failures, and validation of the vendor payload before it reaches the db.
assertions: Identifies the sequential awaits inside the for loop as the cause of the ~22 minute runtime
Identifies `records.forEach(async (rec) => ...)` as never awaited, so writes float and 'done' logs early
Identifies the un-awaited, un-caught top-level `sync()` call as why cron sees success on failure
Uses bounded concurrency sized to the vendor's 20 req/sec limit rather than an unbounded Promise.all
Adds a per-request timeout or AbortSignal so a hung request cannot stall the job
Adds retry with backoff scoped to transient failures (429/5xx/network) rather than retrying every error
Checks res.ok and/or validates the vendor payload before writing it to Postgres
Sets a non-zero process exit code on failure so the cron job reports correctly
